region.text: the three departments of Algeria and the Saharan territories

ledger.note: 1962: Algeria becomes independent. "On 1 July 1962, some 6 million of a total Algerian electorate of 6.5 million cast their ballots"; "De Gaulle pronounced Algeria an independent country on 3 July"; "The Provisional Executive, however, proclaimed 5 July ... as the day of national independence" (the Fifth Republic page: "Algeria became independent on 5 July 1962"). A ceasefire took effect on 18 March 1962 and the French electorate approved the Evian Accords on 8 April 1962.

1962: France keeps three bases in Algeria under the Evian Accords. "the nuclear test site of Regghane, the naval base of Mers-el-Kebir and the air base of Bou Sfer"; only Mers El Kebir is drawn (a 15 km radius is the researcher's reading), since the page does not bound the others.
1967: the last French forces leave Mers El Kebir. "the last French forces did not leave the naval base of Mers El Kebir until 1967" (the page notes this was ahead of the Evian schedule).

1975: the Comoros leave France. "6 July 1975 – Comorian President Ahmed Abdallah declares the whole archipelago independent of France"; "the French refuse to recognise the inclusion of Mayotte in the new state" (French Community page, chronology). Mayotte stays French and became an overseas department on 31 March 2011 (Overseas France page). [Reviewer eu-22-c, 2026-11-01: month and confidence set from the French Community page.]

ledger.note: 1977: the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas becomes independent as Djibouti on 27 June. Infobox "Independence: 27 June 1977"; it had been renamed from French Somaliland in 1967, after the plebiscite of 19 March 1967, and a third vote took place on 8 May 1977.

wars.name: Algerian War
wars.outcome: "Algerian victory" (infobox, 1 November 1954 - 19 March 1962): the Evian Accords, approved by the French electorate on 8 April 1962 and by the Algerian referendum of 1 July 1962, gave independence, proclaimed on 5 July 1962.
wars.note: No contest_start/contest_end is recorded: the FLN held no mapped ground that the pages bound. The war moved the border once, by the 1962 loss of Algeria. The Fifth Republic began in the middle of it (the May 1958 crisis returned de Gaulle).

certainty.note: Researcher's judgment, no page opened on frontiers: the African, Malagasy and Saharan colonial boundaries were administrative lines; metropolitan France and the departments are sharp.
Metropolitan frontiers and overseas coasts are treaty and survey lines; the Saharan and Caribbean/Pacific islands are small enough to be sharp.

notes: Five pages for France (budget up to 5) plus two pages opened for the German dossiers. The Cliopatria row is a Community-wide outline for 1958-1960 and a 2024 outline plus Algeria, Djibouti and the Comoros for 1961-2023. The 1961-2023 shape contained Algeria (8,752 cells); corrected by splitting into 1961-62, 1963-77 and 1978-2023 keyframes. The shapes have no cell of French Polynesia, Wallis and Futuna or Saint Pierre and Miquelon (gazetteer check against country masks) and the 2024 shape lacks them too; added in every correction. Saint-Martin (53 km2) and Saint-Barthelemy (25 km2) are below the grid. Client tint: the Community members are drawn as clients from their autonomy (Oct-Dec 1958) to independence (1960); that reading is the researcher's, the pages say "autonomous states within the Community". The Comoros event is dated 6 July 1975 at confidence 3 from the French Community chronology (corrected by the reviewer of eu-22-c; the author had read the page as silent). The Comoros and Bizerte: the Tunisian dossier (af-08, another group) records the Bizerte crisis (contest 1961-07, evacuation 1963-10) with France as counterpart; not opened here (page budget), so France's side of it is a gap for the reviewer. Counterparts: comoros has no Cliopatria row or dossier on 2026-11-01 (listed in the report). The ledger holds the 1958-1960 decolonisation month by month because the Cliopatria 1960 shape cannot show it. Guinea is not a loss of the Fifth Republic (it left two days before the constitution; the guinea dossier records its own found). The gazetteer finds no cell of Vanuatu or of Indochina in any of the four Cliopatria shapes. Mayotte, Saint-Martin and Saint-Barthelemy changed status but not sovereignty.
